title: Aethusa Cynapium
text: The characteristic symptoms are related to the brain and the nervous system, with gastro-intestinal disturbance. It is especially indicated in children during dentition and in summer complaints. The child is unable to digest milk, which is vomited in large, sour curds. Great weakness and sleepiness after vomiting or stool. Indigestion of teething children. Inability to think, to fix the attention. Idiocy in children. Inability to think, to fix the attention. Confused. Anxiety and restlessness. Hallucinations. Fears death. Headache, with a sensation as if the head were in a vice. Vertigo, with sleepiness. Weight in the occiput. Pupils dilated. Eyes turned downward. Photophobia. Expression of great anxiety and pain. Linea nasalis marked. Pale face. Dryness of the mouth. Aphthae. Tongue feels as if too long. Intolerance of milk; it is vomited in large, sour curds, or as soon as swallowed. Regurgitation of food an hour after eating. Violent vomiting of white, frothy matter. Great thirst. Distended and tense. Coldness of the abdomen. Diarrhoea of thin, yellow-greenish, or bloody mucus. Tenesmus. Much weakness and sleepiness after stool. Worse in the morning and from milk. Better in the open air. Compare: Antimon. crud.; Cicuta; Calcarea carbonica. Third to thirtieth potency.
